subject: Post-incident: log escrow options, slicing window, and deletion checklist
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2025-06-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: initial questions on logs for Acme incident

Hi Irene — thanks again for the quick turnaround on the incident summary. A couple follow-ups from our security team about retention and transfer:

- How long will the full request/response traces be retained in the primary bucket for the incident? We need to understand the maximum window before deletion.
- Can you provide a path for an escrow or short-term export (48-72 hours) of the preserved logs for our internal forensics team?
- Is there a supported workflow for redacting PII before transfer? If not, what tooling do you recommend?

We may need a copy under our custodian controls for evidence. Appreciate a quick note on options — rough timelines are fine.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Security, Acme Corp

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: initial questions on logs for Acme incident

Elaine — quick summary below, copying Marcus and Karthik for implementation details and custody steps.

1) Retention windows
- Primary hot store: rolling 30 days by default for customer telemetry.
- Incident hold: for this event we have placed a 90-day hold slice for the affected workspace (starts 2025-06-10). That means preserved artifacts will not auto-delete during the hold.

2) Escrow/export options
- We can produce an encrypted snapshot (AES-256, customer KMS wrap) of the relevant partitions. Typical prep/packaging time: 24–48 hours. Transfer options: secure SFTP, customer S3 (signed bucket policy), or couriered encrypted disk for very large archives.

3) Redaction and PII
- We offer server-side redaction tooling for common identifiers (emails, SSNs, IPs) as a pre-transfer pass. It produces a manifest and a redaction report. For legal/forensics needs we recommend retaining an unredacted master under a sealed chain-of-custody with restricted access; let us know if Acme requests that.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus: please confirm snapshot ETA and include a minimal manifest (file counts + byte sizes).
- Karthik: confirm chain-of-custody packaging steps and whether we can set a short-term escrow (48–72h) to a customer-managed S3.

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T13:25:00Z
Subject: Re: initial questions on logs for Acme incident

Irene / team — implementation notes and constraints below. Quoting parts for clarity.

On retention windows:
- Confirm we currently have the workspace on a 90-day incident hold; manifest generated at 2025-06-12T12:00Z.

On export/escrow:
- ETA: we can surface a packaged snapshot within 36 hours if we scope to the relevant time window and indices. Packaging includes: index metadata, segment files, and KV cache dumps. Archive will be encrypted with customer KMS key if provided, otherwise we use Redwood-managed wrap and provide access logs.
- Transfer mechanics: recommend customer S3 upload (we produce presigned multipart upload tokens with bucket lifecycle disabled during transfer). For SFTP we can push to an endpoint; note we throttle large exports to avoid impacting live serving.

On redaction:
- Server-side redaction is available but not exhaustive; our tooling flags likely PII patterns and replaces them with deterministic tokens. We will also produce a redaction map file and a redaction-audit.txt artifact. If Acme requires full manual review, that'll add 24–48 hours.

On chain-of-custody and escrow lifecycle:
- We can run a chain-of-custody form (attached) and produce a signed manifest. The recommended plan: escrow snapshot to Acme S3 for 7 days, after sign-off move to an immutable evidence store for 90 days (customer choice). If Acme wants us to delete after N days, provide the requested retention and we'll schedule deletion.

Attachments: forensic-archive-inventory.csv.gz (inventory of shards), chain_of_custody-form.pdf

Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-13T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: packaging and deletion checklist for Acme evidence transfer

Elaine — following up with the proposed minimal checklist so your legal/forensics teams can sign off quickly. Please confirm which transfer option you prefer (customer S3 or SFTP).

Proposed checklist (minimal acceptance criteria):
1) Scope:
   - Time window: 2025-06-09T00:00:00Z through 2025-06-10T23:59:59Z
   - Indices: request-traces-v2, auth-events, session-metrics
2) Packaging:
   - Format: gzipped tarball with manifest.csv and per-file SHA256 checksums
   - Encryption: AES-256; KMS key: (customer-provided preferred)
3) Redaction:
   - Default: PII tokenization pass + redaction-map included
   - Optional: provide legal-approved regex list for additional redactions
4) Transfer and escrow:
   - Transfer target: acme-incident-escrow (customer S3)
   - Escrow window: 7 days by default; can be shortened to 48–72h for expedited teardown
5) Post-transfer deletion
   - Redwood will schedule deletion from hot store 7 days after transfer completion unless customer requests extended hold (provide signed request)
6) Evidence retention and legal hold
   - If Acme issues a legal hold, Redwood will mark artifacts as preserved and pause deletion.

Marissa — can you draft the short form custody letter and a one-page redaction brief (for their legal) and share the Drive link?

Karthik
Head of Forensics and Incident Response
Redwood Inference
